A.holding_summary: A traveling salesman who stayed at a hotel three or four days each week and left his trunk in the hotel's storage room between stays was a guest while there; the storage was a bailment for mutual benefit rather than an innkeeper's strict liability, and the hotel was liable for the lost trunk on failing to show ordinary care. The court treated the hotel's weekly accommodation of the guest as ordinary lawful innkeeping.

Under this state of facts, therefore, the plaintiff established a bailment by special arrangement for storage of baggage, for the mutual benefit of bailor and bailee, and the bailee became liable for the exercise of ordinary care for its safety.

A lessor out of possession and control is not liable to a tenant for personal injuries absent deceit, agreement, or statute.

D.holding_summary: Township ordinance licensing individual owner-occupied trailers parked on the owner's own land held ultra vires under R.S. 40:52-1(d). The court read the statute (hotels, boarding houses, lodging and rooming houses, trailer camps) as authorizing licensing only of businesses and public sleeping/lodging places affected with a public interest, not private dwellings. No letting for pay was at issue; the passage treats lodging houses as regulable businesses while protecting the private owner-occupant.

quotes.text: This act provides purely and plainly for the regulation and licensing of businesses and public sleeping, lodging and eating places where regulation is a necessity in order to protect and promote the health, safety, morals and general welfare of the community. The municipality has no authority under this statute to license the owners of individual trailers parked on the owner’s land, not affected with a public interest, nor clothed with a public use.

The ordinance and the amendment thereto is illegal and void insofar as it attempts to license a trailer and the owner thereof who uses the same for sleeping and eating purposes while parked on his own property.

quotes.text: The defendants owned a three-family house in the city of Hartford and they resided on the first floor. The plaintiff visited the property and entered into a parol lease from month to month on the assurance of the defendants that they would attend to necessary repairs.

At common law as a general rule, the landlord is under no implied obligation or liability to the tenant for personal injuries due to the defective condition of the demised premises or the lack of repair of defects therein where the landlord has not made any warranty or contract relative to the condition of the demised premises or the repair of defects.
When a landlord retains control of the premises for the purpose of keeping them in repair he must exercise reasonable care through inspection to keep the premises in a reasonably safe condition.

D.holding_summary: Zoning ordinance excluding sanitariums for nervous diseases from residential districts is a valid police-power measure as to new establishments, but is invalid as applied to existing, lawfully operating sanitariums because a retroactive ordinance destroying a non-nuisance business without compensation is an unreasonable exercise of the police power.

quotes.text: The decisions uphold the validity of ordinances excluding from residential districts property uses much less incongruous than these, as, for example, fiats, stores and business buildings.

Our-conclusion is that where, as here, a retroactive .ordinance causes substantial injury and the prohibited business^ is not a nuisance, the ordinance is to that extent an unreasonable and unjustifiable exercise of police power.

It follows that the present ordinance is valid in so far as it prohibits the further establishment of businesses of this type in the restricted districts; and is invalid in its application to these plaintiffs.

If we do so on the ground that this is a proper exercise of the police power in the enactment of zoning legislation, then it follows that the same thing may be done to apartment houses, flats, or stores.
The approval of such a. doctrine would be a blow to rights in private property such as this court has never before witnessed.

In other words, the obligation of the landlord is said to be limited to the extent of the privilege conferred upon the tenant.

F.holding_summary: A verbal lease of a dwelling for a term not exceeding three years, accompanied by possession, is taken out of the statute of frauds and binds both parties as if written. In forcible entry and detainer the tenant may prove the terms of the parol lease by parol evidence; exclusion of such evidence was prejudicial error.

quotes.text: It being tbe settled law of this state that a verbal lease for a term not exceeding three years, when accompanied by possession, is taken out of the statute of frauds, it follows that the duration and terms of the parol lease may be shown by evidence of the verbal agreement between the parties.

“If a lease is not in writing but a mere verbal contract, it is binding on both parties, provided the tenant took possession under it, precisely as if it was executed according to the prescribed rules of the statute. ’ ”

Plaintiff in error sought to show, this proceeding having been brought about six months after their occupancy began, that, before possession of the premises were taken, conversations were had between plaintiff and defendants of such a character that a parol lease for one year was agreed upon.
